intro: You are standing at the Church of Saint Peter, a monastery and church in Hatay province from the 1st century AD. This cave church, cut into the mountainside, is held to be where the community of Antioch met: the first people anywhere to be called Christians.
history: This cave church, cut into the slope of Mount Staurin, is held to be where the first Christian community of Antioch gathered. According to Acts, it was in this city that believers were first called Christians. Look at the façade: it was added in the crusader period. And in 1963 the papacy declared the church a place of pilgrimage.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the cave nave and the crusader façade, look down at the floor mosaic, and find the escape tunnel.
facts: Did you know? A tunnel runs from the back of the church into the mountain, thought to have been cut so that the congregation could escape a raid. And according to Acts, it was in this city that believers were first called Christians.
outro: This brings our journey through the Church of Saint Peter to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
